o.text:
Etymology tree
Arabic آمَنَ (ʔāmana)
Arabic إِيمَان (ʔīmān)bor.
Azerbaijani iman
Borrowed from Arabic إِيمَان (ʔīmān), from آمَنَ (ʔāmana).
Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *dil-. Analyzable as *dilmək + -im. See more at dilmek.
From Arabic عَوَامّ (ʕawāmm), plural of Arabic عَامَّة (ʕāmma, “common people”).
From Turkish kimlik. By surface analysis, kim (“who”) + -lik (“-ness”).
From Proto-Turkic *koguĺ. See more cognates at Bashkir ҡыуыш (qıwış).
Borrowed from Turkish dergi, where it was reintroduced as a learned borrowing from Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (dẹrgü, “tablecloth, napery”).
Izafet II compound of komendant + saat. Calque of Russian коменда́нтский ча́с (komendántskij čás).
